lessons.title: What’s your favourite sport?
lessons.kind: 对话 · 李明与宋华在操场上聊各自最喜欢的运动
canonical: Li Ming and Song Hua are talking about sports on the playground.
What’s your favourite sport, Song Hua?
Hmm... I like basketball, but I think swimming is my favourite.
I feel free when I’m in the water.
I started learning to swim at the age of five, and I still go to the pool every Saturday evening.
That sounds great! What are some benefits of swimming?
Swimming helps me stay in shape, improves my endurance, and reduces my stress.
After swimming, I always feel refreshed.
How about you, Li Ming? What’s your favourite sport?
For me, it’s ping-pong.
It improves my motor skills and my hand-eye coordination.
I practice it at the sports centre on weekends, and I have made some friends there.
We all love ping-pong and have a lot of fun together.
Sports help us improve our physical abilities, learn new skills, overcome challenges, and build confidence.
Well said! Look! There is a basketball game going on. Let’s go and cheer them!

lessons.title: National sport
lessons.kind: 说明文 · 乒乓球为什么是中国的国球
canonical: Ping-pong, also known as table tennis, holds a special place in Chinese people’s hearts. It shows our love for sports and the spirit of never giving up.
It inspires young athletes and brings joy and a feeling of community to every player.
Ping-pong has deep historical roots in China. The game became popular in the early 20th century.
Now, people of all ages play this sport in gyms, parks, community centres, and even at home.
Ping-pong is a fast-paced sport. It can improve your overall physical fitness.
Ping-pong uses both the left and right sides of the brain. So it can also improve your memory and problem-solving skills. What a fun national sport!
Since ping-pong entered the Olympics in 1988, the Chinese ping-pong team has won many gold medals.
The team has also had many great victories in major ping-pong events, such as the World Championship and the World Cup.
The achievements of Chinese players on the global stage have inspired many people.
Ping-pong has already become an important part of our culture.
The game serves as exercise and as a way for people to connect with others. Don’t wait! Go play ping-pong with your friends.

lessons.title: Dream team
lessons.kind: 说明文 · 梦之队的含义与各国的梦之队
canonical: At the 1992 Olympics, the US basketball team won the gold medal. People called it the dream team.
Nowadays a dream team refers to the greatest team in its field.
There have been many dream teams throughout the history of sports.
Canada’s dream team plays on ice — it’s the country’s ice hockey team.
For Brazil, it might be the men’s volleyball or soccer team.
What is China’s dream team? Many people would think of the diving team.
China also has dream teams in ping-pong and weight lifting. Time after time, these teams have won gold medals for China.
However, there is more to a dream team than winning gold medals.
A dream team has not only the best players and the best coach, but also the best team spirit.
All of the players must work hard and cooperate with one another.
By working together, they show their courage and their drive. They never give up. That’s what makes a dream team!
The spirit of a dream team influences lots of people everywhere, not only in their home nation.
People admire and feel proud of their dream team.

lessons.title: Never giving up
lessons.kind: 记叙文 · 球迷讲述中国女排精神对自己的影响
canonical: I’m a huge fan of the Chinese women’s volleyball team.
I have watched nearly all of their games and have often found myself cheering or shedding tears with the players during these matches.
Throughout the years, I have seen this team win many championships and bring glory and pride to our nation.
What makes the Chinese women’s volleyball team special? It is their determination, teamwork, and spirit.
No matter how tough things get, they never give up. When a player misses a shot, the teammates don’t blame her.
Instead, they come together and offer words of encouragement. They support each other and create a positive and exciting atmosphere on the court.
Whether they win or lose, they stay united as a team. The coach, Lang Ping, once said, “Volleyball is not just a job; it is our whole life.”
And the team members truly live by that.
The team’s spirit has had a strong influence on me. When I come across difficulty or challenge, their never-give-up spirit always motivates me to keep trying.
The team has taught me to do my best in everything. I have also learned the value of teamwork from them.
Working with others and supporting each other can lead to amazing achievements.

lessons.title: Classroom Olympics
lessons.kind: 电子邮件 · Jenny 向王梅介绍班级教室奥运会
canonical: We had our own classroom Olympics this week! Our class had five different events — jump rope, long jump, sit-ups, push-ups, and “ping-pong pass”.
Everyone competed in each event, one by one.
The events were fun! Kim won first place in the jump rope event. She jumped 178 times in one minute without stopping.
Lisa won second place in the long jump. She jumped very far, but Kim jumped farther.
My favourite event was “ping-pong pass”. Each student had to balance a ping-pong ball with chopsticks and move it from one basket to another without dropping it.
We used a stopwatch to see who was the fastest. You know what? I can use chopsticks very well.
Tom did his best, but his ping-pong ball kept falling off his chopsticks.
What were the results? I won the race! David was only two seconds slower than me.
It’s really enjoyable to do sports with friends! I like classroom Olympics. What about you?

lessons.title: The Olympic Games
lessons.kind: 说明文 · 奥运会的历史、举办城市与旗帜格言
canonical: The Olympic Games were an ancient athletic festival in Greece. Among the games held throughout Greece, the Olympic Games were the most famous.
They were held every four years.
The modern Olympic Games became popular in the late 19th century. In 1892, at a meeting in Paris, Pierre de Coubertin put forward the idea of holding Olympic Games again.
In 1894, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) was founded.
Modern Olympic Games include the Summer Olympics and the Winter Olympics.
The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896, while the first Winter Olympics were held in Chamonix, France, in 1924.
Since 1994, the Olympic Games have alternated between a summer and a winter edition every two years.
In 2008, Beijing became the first Chinese city to host the Games. Do you remember the slogan “One World, One Dream”?
The song You and Me touched many people’s hearts. In 2022, Beijing hosted the Winter Olympic Games.
It became the first city in the world to host both the Summer and the Winter Olympic Games.
The Olympic flag has a white background with five interlaced rings in blue, yellow, black, green, and red.
These rings symbolise the unity of the continents. The motto of the Olympic Games is “Faster, Higher, Stronger — Together”.
